bolt.notes: Checked 2026-07-17: PRs #530, #534, #541, #573, #580, #590, #595 (title-prefixed "⚡ Bolt:") all show author.login = RB-chrismandich (is_bot: false) via `gh pr list --json author`, and their commits[].authors are the same account (`gh pr view <N> --json commits`). Same situation as palette: Bolt is a Jules persona, not a distinct GitHub bot account — identify by the "⚡ Bolt:" title prefix and/or "bolt/" branch prefix. Live-verified 2026-07-17: `gh pr list --search "head:bolt-"` returns 0 results; `gh pr list --search "head:bolt/"` returns the real open Bolt PRs (#590, #595). Only #580 used the older "bolt-" convention — 6 of 7 cited PRs plus both currently-open ones use "bolt/", so that's the value this field must carry to actually match anything today. Focus: performance micro-optimizations (fast-path checks, avoided re-parses/re-reads).

clarity.notes:
Added 2026-08-07 after a pr-triage-bots run on RB-chrismandich/whycast surfaced five open PRs (#544, #545, #548, #550, #554) that no registry entry matched — the same gap Forge had on 2026-07-27. Fourth Jules persona. Verified via `gh pr list --state all --search "Clarity in:title" --json author`: the persona has 12+ PRs going back to whycast #452. Focus: static-analysis compliance — mypy type narrowing, guard clauses, Optional handling.
Two facts that differ from the palette/bolt entries:
1. author_login is NOT stable across repos or across time. Older Clarity
   PRs (whycast #452, #466, #468, #470, #494, #506, #515) show
   author.login = RB-chrismandich (is_bot: false), matching the
   palette/bolt situation. Newer ones (#541, #544, #545, #548, #550,
   #554) show author.login = "app/google-labs-jules" with is_bot: true
   — the Jules GitHub App was installed on that repo partway through,
   so it now opens PRs under its own identity. The same split is visible
   on Bolt in whycast (#516 = RB-chrismandich, #540/#543/#546/#547 =
   app/google-labs-jules). Do not filter these personas by author;
   the title prefix is the only identifier stable across both eras.

2. branch_prefix has no consistent separator: #545/#548/#554 use
   "clarity/", #544/#550 use "clarity-". Match the bare word, not
   "clarity/".

Triage caution — observed 2026-08-07: Clarity over-produces hard on a single target (5 PRs for one 8-line cli.py fix; #550 and #554 were byte-identical to #548, and #545's per-file hunk hashed identical too). It also reaches for `(events or [])` fallbacks to silence Optional errors (#544), which converts a failure into a silent empty iteration — check its diffs against the repo's silent-failure conventions before merging, and prefer the variant using explicit `is None` guards.

copilot.notes: Verified 2026-07-17 via `gh api repos/RB-chrismandich/Manifest/pulls/<N>/reviews` on PRs #533, #538, #543, #550, #554, #559, #563 — login confirmed copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot], displays as "Copilot" in the UI. Reviews land automatically when repo/org settings enable Copilot code review; if neither requested-reviewers nor submitted-reviews show it, the phase is a no-op (don't try to force it — it's a repo/org setting, not something a comment can summon).

forge.notes: Added 2026-07-27 after a pr-triage-bots run surfaced PRs #649 and #651 (title-prefixed "🛠️ Forge:"), neither of which any registry entry matched. Both show author.login = RB-chrismandich (is_bot: false) via `gh pr list --json author` — the same situation as palette and bolt, so Forge is treated as a third Jules persona rather than a distinct GitHub bot account. There is no "forge[bot]" login to verify; asserting one would be a guess. Identify these PRs by the "🛠️ Forge:" title prefix and/or "forge/" branch prefix. Branch names carry a long random numeric suffix (e.g. forge/fix-json-type-checks-eval-15803128462631602317), so match the prefix, never the whole name. Focus: correctness/compliance micro-edits (type narrowing, comment wording, whitespace reflow). Triage caution — observed 2026-07-27: titles overstate the diff (#651 claimed "explicit instructions" for a pure line-rejoin), and edits may target paths that have since moved (both PRs wrote to `.retired skill supply/`, removed by feature 522). Judge the diff against current main, not the title.

jules.label: jules
jules.notes: Apply the jules label (case insensitive) to a GitHub issue to start work, after authorizing the Jules GitHub App for that repository. Jules comments on the issue and links its PR when finished. Verified against https://jules.google/docs/running-tasks/ on 2026-09-07. PR monitoring handles existing Jules feedback; it never labels linked issues or posts trigger mentions. CLI submission is a separate alternative, not an additional trigger for the same issue. Account login does not prove App authorization.

palette.notes: Checked 2026-07-17: PRs #535, #539, #540, #555, #564, #581, #589, #594 (title-prefixed "🎨 Palette:") all show author.login = RB-chrismandich (is_bot: false) via `gh pr list --json author`, and their commits[].authors are the same account (`gh pr view <N> --json commits`). Palette is a Jules persona (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-14-jules-trigger-workflow-design.md; .jules/palette.md is its learning journal) — it opens PRs under whichever account's credentials invoked the Jules session, not a separate bot account. There is no "palette[bot]" GitHub login to verify or refute; asserting one would be a guess, not a fact. Identify these PRs by the "🎨 Palette:" title prefix and/or "palette/" branch prefix instead. Focus: CLI/terminal UX polish (colors, spacing, semantic status icons).
